title.value: Trajectory of Mini-Batch Momentum: Batch Size Saturation and Convergence in High Dimensions
title.justification: The paper thoroughly explores the dynamics of mini-batch stochastic gradient descent with momentum, focusing on batch size saturation and convergence rates in high-dimensional settings.
title.quote: Trajectory of Mini-Batch Momentum: Batch Size Saturation and Convergence in High Dimensions

extractions.description: This paper analyzes the dynamics of large batch stochastic gradient descent with momentum (SGD+M) on the least squares problem in cases where both the number of samples and dimensions are large. The study introduces a deterministic discrete Volterra equation that describes these dynamics. The authors identify a stability measurement called the implicit conditioning ratio (ICR) that determines the ability of SGD+M to accelerate the algorithm. The paper provides explicit choices for the learning rate and momentum parameter that optimize performance and discusses the practical implications of these findings on high-dimensional optimization problems.

primary_category.justification: The paper is focused on the mathematical and algorithmic analysis of stochastic gradient descent with momentum, particularly in the context of optimization in high-dimensional settings. It does not directly address or contribute to any eco-responsible applications or categories such as climate change, pollution, or sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: Despite the wide usage of these stochastic momentum methods in machine learning practice, our understanding of its behaviour is not well–understood.
